posts.title: A free account now includes 10 tasks a day and every category
posts.description: Registered KipFire accounts get 10 free tasks a day across all six categories. Guests get 5 a day. Premium stays unlimited.
posts.body:
A free KipFire account now covers more of the app.

## What a free account includes

You get 10 tasks a day. Those 10 can come from any category: Funny, Challenges, Questions, Would You Rather, Hot Take, or Inner Me. It is one shared limit, not 10 from each category.

## What guests get

Without an account, you get 5 tasks a day, and only Funny and Challenges. After the fifth task, the app offers a free account for the full 10 and the rest of the categories.

## What Premium is for

Premium removes the daily limit. The categories themselves are open on a free account.

The allowance refreshes on a rolling window, not at midnight.

posts.title: How to Start Making Content on Camera: Ideas and What to Say (Beginner Guide 2026)
posts.description: Easy content ideas for beginners, what to say on camera, and why talking head videos with your real face work best in 2026
posts.body:
Want to start making videos but don't know what to film or what to say? You're not alone. Most beginners don't fail because of talent. They fail because they never start, or they quit after two weeks. This guide keeps it simple.
How to start content as a beginner
Use only your phone. No camera, lights, or microphone needed. A quiet room and a window for light is enough.
Film one take. Don't edit for hours. Short and real beats long and perfect.
Keep it 15â€“60 seconds. Short videos are easier to film and easier to watch.
Post 3â€“5 times a week. Consistency matters more than quality at the start.
Don't wait to feel ready. Your first 10 videos will feel awkward. That's normal, and it's how everyone starts.
Content ideas for beginners
Answer a question: "What's one thing you'd tell your younger self?"
Share your opinion: "Hot take: something everyone in my city gets wrong."
Would you rather: "Would you rather lose your phone or your wallet for a week?"
Rate your day from 1 to 10 and explain why.
Tell a small story: the funniest or most awkward thing that happened this week.
Do a quick challenge: "Say 5 things you're grateful for in 10 seconds."
Show your daily life: your job, your gym, your morning coffee, with a short thought.
What to say on camera
If you freeze on camera, use this simple structure:
Hook (first 2 seconds): Say the question or the topic right away. Example: "Would you rather be rich and alone, or broke with real friends?"
Your answer: Say what you really think. Be honest, not perfect.
One reason or story: "Because last year Iâ€¦"
End with a question: "What would you choose? Tell me in the comments."
The easiest trick: don't invent, react. Read a prompt and answer it like you're talking to a friend. Reacting feels natural, so you won't need a script.
Why talking on camera with your real face is best for beginners
It's the fastest format. No editing, no b-roll, no special skills.
People connect with faces. Viewers follow people they recognize and trust, not just information.
It builds your personal brand. Every video makes your face and voice more familiar.
It stands out from AI content. Feeds are filling up with AI-generated videos. Real faces, real emotions and real reactions are becoming rarer, and that's why they'll be worth more.
It builds confidence. Each video makes the next one easier.
The best time to start showing your face is now, while real human content still stands out.
A simple tool to help you start
If you never know what to say, try KipFire, a free iPhone app with prompt cards: questions, challenges, would you rather, hot takes and more. Pick a card, react to it on camera, and the card stays in your video so viewers know what you're answering. One minute, and your video is ready.
Get KipFire on the App Store
FAQ
What should I post if I have no ideas? React to a prompt: a question, a would you rather, or a hot take. It's the easiest way to film without planning.
How do I stop being nervous on camera? Film a lot of short videos. Nervousness drops after your first 10-20 videos.
Do I need to edit my videos? No. For beginners, one-take talking videos work great and save hours.

posts.title: KipFire is on the App Store
posts.description: KipFire is available for iPhone and iPad. Open it, get one short prompt, film your reaction, and post it.
posts.body:
KipFire is on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.

The app gives you one short card to film: a question, a challenge, a hot take, a would-you-rather, a funny line, or an honest line about you. You react on camera. The card sits on the video. The video stays on your phone.

Android is not out yet.

Search for KipFire on the App Store, or use the download button on this site.
